title: An automated 'what's happening on Earth right now' video channel
pitch: Point the live 3D globe at a breaking event, record a dramatic flyover of the real air traffic, ships, or earthquake, then hand that footage to the agentic video studio to script, narrate, and edit it into a finished 60-second explainer. One person runs a daily news-in-motion channel with no camera crew and no editor: the globe supplies real, cinematic footage, and the studio turns it into a polished, captioned video for pennies.
why_now: Both are free and open-source, short-form 'explain the news visually' content is exploding, and together they replace a footage budget and an editing team with two prompts.
